article_notes: Indian study (YSR and Krishna districts; college hospital and several clinics) of 620 dogs tested, 136 with B. gibsoni babesiosis on smear, 11 classed as cerebral babesiosis (PCR-confirmed). Only signalment distributions are given for cerebral cases vs all cases; no laboratory markers compared. Neurological examination (Table 1) describes cerebral cases only. Text gives 8.08% and 8.09% for the same proportion.

severity_definitions.label: cerebral babesiosis vs all dogs with babesiosis
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs with babesiosis (B. gibsoni, smear; PCR in the 11 neurological cases) showing neurological signs were classed as cerebral babesiosis; methods/abstract also cite Babesia in red cells of cerebrospinal fluid. The comparison group is all 136 babesiosis dogs, which includes the 11 cerebral cases.
severity_definitions.comparison_group: all dogs with babesiosis (n=136, includes the 11)
severity_definitions.quote: In this study, 11 of 136 positive Babesia individuals displayed neurological symptoms and were categorized as cerebral babesiosis.

associations.statistic: 0-1 y: 3/11 cerebral vs 14/136 all babesiosis; other age groups for cerebral cases: 2/11 (1-4 y), 3/11 (4-7 y), 1/11 (7-10 y), 2/11 (10-13 y), 0 (>13 y); all babesiosis 48/136, 29/136, 19/136, 17/136, 9/136
associations.quote: Cerebral babesiosis was identified in 27.27 percent (3/11), 18.18 percent (2/11), 27.27 percent (3/11), 9.09 percent (1/11), and 18.18 percent (2/11) of dogs across the relevant age categories
associations.note: Comparison values from the preceding sentence (age distribution of all 136 babesiosis dogs). Comparison group contains the cerebral cases. No test; direction read from printed percentages for the 0-1 year group only.

associations.quote: Cerebral babesiosis showed that 63.63 percent (7/11) of cases were in male dogs, whereas 36.36 percent (4/11) were in female dogs.
associations.note: Comparison value from the preceding sentence. No test; proportions similar.
